nodes.label: LLM Bakeoff Eval Design Spec
nodes.author: Suhaas Surapaneni
nodes.rationale: The spec every `section N.N` reference in the codebase points at. Companion to Model_Bakeoff_Plan.md; it measures and does not decide, and its primary deliverable is an immutable event log rather than a score.

nodes.label: Model-neutrality rule
nodes.rationale: No experimental parameter may be calibrated to a single model. Where a value must come from somewhere it comes from the slowest or broadest case across all four arms, so no model is advantaged by having set the ruler. Sonnet 5 is an arm, not the answer key.

nodes.label: Primary deliverable: the immutable event log
nodes.rationale: Scores are derived views over the log. Re-running 2,000 agentic sessions is expensive and the models will have changed by then, but re-scoring a preserved log is free -- so any metric not captured at run time is lost permanently.

nodes.label: Contamination-free private task set
nodes.rationale: An internal eval on Pindrop's private repos has one property no public benchmark has: the tasks have never been in any model's training data. Named as the strongest methodological claim available.

nodes.label: Four-source task join (ticket, PR, transcript, base_sha)
nodes.rationale: Branch name plus timestamp is the join key into PR history. Known gap: transcripts record gitBranch but no commit SHA, so exact codebase state is recovered lossily by correlating timestamps against git log -- a SessionStart hook stamping `git rev-parse HEAD` is the forward fix.

nodes.label: Task classes A gold / B mined / C agent-only
nodes.rationale: Every task carries the real merged PR diff as reference without exception, which converts the judge's question from open-ended 'is this diff good?' (Cohen's kappa ~0.32) into reference-anchored 'does this accomplish what the reference accomplished?'. The dataset, not the judge prompt, is what makes judging accurate.

nodes.label: One-instruction prompt construction
nodes.rationale: One human instruction, then autonomous turns: reads, edits, runs tests, sees failures, self-corrects. Multi-turn human corrections are not replayed because they were conditioned on the original model's output; they are repurposed as judge rubric items instead.

nodes.label: No LLM user-simulator
nodes.rationale: Rejected despite precedent (tau-bench, AA's tau3-Banking): it confounds model with simulator, and a useful simulator needs the answer, which leaks unevenly -- a floundering model draws more corrective detail, actively compensating weak models and inverting what the eval measures.

nodes.label: Stratification to measured production distribution
nodes.rationale: Weight strata to a measured transcript stats pass, not a guessed split -- a 50/50 tier split on a workload that is 70% small edits measures the wrong thing and will not transfer to the bill. Includes a long-session stratum because 256K context claims degrade unevenly before the limit.

nodes.label: Calibration pilot and model-neutral drop rule
nodes.rationale: All four models at N=3 across ~80 candidates. Drop only floor (all four score 0%) or ceiling (all four score 100%); keep any task where models disagree, however lopsidedly -- a task only Sonnet solves is among the most informative in the set. Also sets budget caps from the slowest-converging model.

nodes.label: Privacy gate blocking team data collection
nodes.rationale: Engineer consent, secret-scanning over all JSONL, and a retention decision must precede any collection: retrofitting a privacy pass after twenty engineers' transcripts are in a shared bucket is far worse than doing it up front.

nodes.label: Task record schema (§3.7)
nodes.rationale: task_id, tier, stratum, repo, base_sha, image digest, verbatim prompt, reference_diff, f2p/p2p sets, rubric items and provenance. This is the shape task.yaml manifests implement.

nodes.label: Nine deterministic checks (resolved gate)
nodes.rationale: Run in order, first failure short-circuits and sets failure_class. `resolved` = all nine pass, binary, no partial credit -- that is what removes grader subjectivity. Deterministic checks gate; the judge only ranks, and a run failing the gate gets no quality score at all.

nodes.label: Test-file restoration from base_sha (primary anti-cheat)
nodes.rationale: Without `git checkout <base_sha> -- <test paths>` before grading, 'make the tests pass' is trivially satisfied by deleting or weakening tests, and models do this at different rates -- so it would register as a capability difference. Whether the agent modified tests is recorded separately, never silently dropped.

nodes.label: Score construction: pass@1, pass^k, paired analysis
nodes.rationale: resolve_rate is the headline and subgoal_rate breaks ties, never blended -- weighted partial credit would reintroduce the grader subjectivity all-or-nothing scoring exists to remove. Analysis is always paired: task difficulty is common to both arms and cancels in the per-task difference.

nodes.label: Judge protocol (rubric profile + blind pairwise)
nodes.rationale: Five orthogonal dimensions on a 3-point anchored scale (1-10 scales show poor inter-rater agreement), plus round-robin blind position-randomized pairwise converted to Elo. Pair sample i against sample i -- pairing a draw against another model's best or median compares a draw to a statistic and skews the win rate.

nodes.label: Judge configuration: neutral family, evidence-fed, calibrated
nodes.rationale: A Claude judge inflates Sonnet 5 and a Gemini judge inflates Gemma, so the judge must sit outside all four families -- GPT-class, with the third-party egress tradeoff reviewed and accepted. If Cohen's kappa against the ~20% human gold subset falls below 0.6, Tier B is directional only and must not carry the decision.

nodes.label: Statistical power: why N=10, not N=3
nodes.rationale: Naive binomial CIs are optimistic and must not be quoted: attempts within a task are correlated, so the honest unpaired half-width is ~±12 pts at 60 tasks, which paired analysis brings to ~±6. Task count drives precision; N drives reliability measurement. Judge noise attenuates effects as 1/(2a-1)^2, which is why reference-anchoring and evidence-feeding are load-bearing.

nodes.label: Optional executable Tier B
nodes.rationale: Authoring acceptance tests (~1-3 hr/task) converts the primary decision signal from kappa~0.32 to deterministic -- the highest-leverage spend available. If pursued the judge is demoted, not removed: it scores attributes that resist encoding as tests and never overrides the executable result.

nodes.label: Start-state pinning (§5.1)
nodes.rationale: Every run begins from a byte-identical world: container by digest not tag, detached checkout at base_sha, lockfile dependencies baked into the image, network off or through a recording proxy, fresh container per sample. State bleed across the N=10 would correlate repeats and silently shrink effective N.

nodes.label: Claude Code configuration control (§5.2)
nodes.rationale: Named the highest-risk contamination source: CLAUDE.md, settings.json, hooks, MCP servers, skills and output styles all substantially change agent behavior, and the operator's environment is heavily customized. The verification half -- dumping and diffing the effective config at session start and storing it in the record -- is what makes the claim checkable.

nodes.label: Frozen sampling parameters (§5.3)
nodes.rationale: Temperature 0 for non-reasoning, 0.6 or lab-recommended for reasoning, recorded per run. The '(or lab-recommended)' clause is load-bearing -- what is held identical across arms is the policy, not the number.

nodes.label: Budget policy: generous caps, measure actuals (§5.4)
nodes.rationale: Caps derive from the slowest-converging model's p95 x2, not the incumbent's -- tuning to Sonnet 5's turn distribution converts a style difference into a capability score. Every cap unit favors someone (wall-clock favors fast models, turns favor verbose ones, tokens favor terse ones), so cap on turns and tokens together and record which limit terminated each run.

nodes.label: Checkpointing: the cost/quality curve for free (§5.5)
nodes.rationale: One generous-cap run yields the pass rate at any budget K post-hoc -- same information as separate capped runs at half the compute. Stored as incremental diffs against base_sha, never worktrees. Grading is a decoupled offline batch because inline would be ~96,000 suite executions.

nodes.label: End-state extraction (§5.6)
nodes.rationale: `git add -A && git diff --cached <base_sha>` in the container after termination. Never trust the agent's self-report -- agents claim false success at different rates per model, which would itself become a fake signal. Staging first normalizes over whether the agent committed, left the tree dirty, or created new files.

nodes.label: Randomized, interleaved execution order (§5.7)
nodes.rationale: Sequential per-model batches confound model identity with Bedrock regional load, network conditions and host contention -- which makes latency, a stated success criterion, uninterpretable. Execution timestamp is treated as an analysis covariate.

nodes.label: Prompt-cache warming as an asymmetric cost confound (§5.8)
nodes.rationale: Sonnet 5 has prompt caching and the candidates' Bedrock cache support is unconfirmed, so batched repeats would make Sonnet artificially cheap and bias cost-per-completed-workflow against the very candidates the eval exists to evaluate. Controls: interleave, log cache_state.warm and the prior same-task run id, report cost both raw and cache-normalized.

nodes.label: Per-run record (§6.1)
nodes.rationale: The full field list the harness dataclasses implement: versions block, config digest, timing split into inference vs tool_exec, per-turn token records required for the cost-at-budget-K curve, checkpoints, tool call stats, failure_class, destructive events, host metrics and artifact paths.

nodes.label: Mandatory wire-level logging (§6.2)
nodes.rationale: Without the full pre-parse request/response payload, `malformed: true` is a dead end -- you cannot tell whether the fault was LiteLLM's tool translation or the model. That distinction is the difference between 'fix the adapter and retest' and 'drop the model', the single most consequential call the eval has to make.

nodes.label: Judge and human-grader records (§6.3)
nodes.rationale: Stored separately and linked by run_id, carrying the exact input_payload and shown_payload. Without those and time_spent_s a disputed kappa cannot be re-examined -- and because judge inputs are logged, swapping the judge is a re-score rather than a re-run.

nodes.label: Exclusion policy (§6.4)
nodes.rationale: Exclusion is the one mechanism by which results get massaged, even honestly. Criteria are written down before the run, every excluded run keeps its full record, and the exclusion rate is reported per model because asymmetry is itself a finding.

nodes.label: Adapter-failure exclusion class
nodes.rationale: Genuinely ambiguous: adapter failures are fixable going forward AND they are the production path. So headline results are published with and without them, always both, never collapsed into one number.

nodes.label: Logger verification gate (§6.6 fault injection)
nodes.rationale: Twelve fault-injection cases that must each produce a complete, correctly-classified record. The logger is trusted with 2,400 runs, so it is tested before rather than after. Closed 2026-08-06; working the list found four defects the originally-drafted tests would have passed over.

nodes.label: Phase plan 0 through 6
nodes.rationale: Deliberately reordered so data capture precedes scoring -- scoring reads the log and never gates collection. Total ~3.5-4.5 weeks against the plan doc's 2.5-3; the delta is the instrumentation phase and N=10, which are what make the result defensible.

nodes.label: Phase 0c end-to-end smoke test (go/no-go)
nodes.rationale: If a candidate cannot drive Claude Code at all through LiteLLM, that must surface on day one rather than in week three after the dataset is built. A failure is not necessarily disqualifying -- it may be an adapter issue -- but it changes the plan immediately. Also sizes the compute plan.

nodes.label: Cost baseline open item (§8)
nodes.rationale: The plan's $5,000/month baseline assumes zero caching, but a representative transcript record shows ~99.99% of input billed as cache reads at 0.1x list. If candidates lack Bedrock caching while the baseline has it, true savings is materially smaller and possibly small enough to change the recommendation -- a blocking input, not a footnote.

nodes.label: Stated limitations (§9)
nodes.rationale: To appear in the writeup, not buried: autonomous single-instruction is harder than real usage (a lower bound), the task set is Pindrop-specific by intent, Tier B judgment is low-resolution by nature, harness fit is confounded with capability, and transcript-derived tasks skew toward already-agent-suitable work.

nodes.label: Scorecard, not a composite (§10)
nodes.rationale: Collapsing rows into one number hides the tradeoff and renders the result unfalsifiable; a scorecard forces the tradeoff into the open where it can be argued with. Any metric reported without a confidence interval is not reported.

nodes.label: Reference points, not gates (OPEN-8)
nodes.rationale: Four of six thresholds are defaults with nothing behind them, so they are annotations on the scorecard rather than pass/fail criteria. Promotion to decision criteria must happen before results exist, never after.

nodes.label: OPEN-10 destructive-event severity scale
nodes.rationale: §6.1 used `severity` without defining levels. Resolution: high = unreverted data/history loss or secret exposure, medium = reverted or contained, low = risky but no effect.

nodes.label: Storage (§6.5)
nodes.rationale: Gzipped trajectories and wire logs, incremental checkpoint diffs, container stdout/stderr, test output and full judge records -- low tens of GB for 2,400 runs, cheap insurance relative to re-running. Private repo or bucket with a documented access list, secret-scanned on write because wire logs and trajectories both contain repository source.
